instruction: Bold the title on slide 5 and set its font size to 36pt.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully bolded all text on slide 1, changed title to 44pt, and underlined it in 14 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select text in LibreOffice Impress, apply bold/underline formatting, change font size via character properties panel.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests bold and font size formatting on a different slide (slide 5), requiring navigation to another slide first.
metadata.explanation: Getter reads slide 5 title ('Infographic Slide Report') runs for bold and size_pt. Metric awards 0.5 for all runs bold=True and 0.5 for all runs at 36pt.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets slide 5 (index 4) and identifies the title shape by searching for 'Infographic' in text, matching the confirmed title 'Infographic Slide Report'.
Metric correctly checks both instruction requirements: bold (all runs bold=True for 0.5 points) and font size (all runs at 36pt with 0.5pt tolerance for 0.5 points).
Metric correctly handles expected parameter — directly accesses expected.get('expected_size_pt', 36.0) from the rules dict, consistent with get_rule behavior.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 + 0.5) is appropriate for a two-requirement task.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The getter identifies the title by hardcoded text match ('Infographic' in shape.text). Consider also checking shape.placeholder_format or shape type for more robust title detection, though this is sufficient for this specific task.

Minor: run.font.bold can be None (inherited from style) rather than True. If the presentation's slide master already has bold on the title style, the agent might not need to explicitly set bold, and the getter would return None instead of True. This edge case is unlikely but worth noting.
